correctness.rationale: For any positive-weight Jacobi path, the eigenvector–eigenvalue cofactor identity converts the Krylov determinant squared to |Res(p,p_left p_right)|. Two characteristic-polynomial reductions and successive tridiagonal resultants evaluate this as the edge-monomial square times |Res(p_left,p_right)| squared, including shared-root zeros. Distinct eigenvalues and independence of exponentials yield the positive common finite-horizon kernel; the Cauchy determinant gives positive-damping infinite horizon. For five mirror-symmetric vertices, direct exact symbolic evaluation gives endpoint factors a^5 b^5, adjacent interior factors a^4 b^5 |a-2b|, and midpoint zero, proving the strict b=a boundary. The extracted verifier ran 200 supplementary checks, including all five symbolic factors and three phase regimes; no finite experiment serves as the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: Compared full statements and implications. Parlangeli–Notarstefano and a previously recorded unweighted-path result cover rank and the all-order uniform determinant tie: these are excluded from new scope. Dilip (2019) establishes the general symmetric spectral-Gramian factorization and a P6 example. Liu–Shan (2026) develops rooted-resultant machinery and fixed uniform-parameter central path cases; the complete public four-node weighted-path paper already covers n=4. The new claim is specifically an arbitrary-length, all-vertex, arbitrary-independent-positive-weight product of explicit edge monomials and two principal-block resultants, plus a complete n=5 nonuniform mirror-symmetric phase. None of the inspected full sources states these; equivalent historical Jacobi-polynomial formulas remain a material priority risk.
residual_risks: A weighted Jacobi-rooted controllability determinant or corresponding orthogonal-polynomial resultant may already appear in unindexed historic literature; general algebraic tools are established.

Dilip (2019) already proves horizon-independent spectral determinant placement. Earlier unweighted-path all-size equal determinants are known from an accessible own historical claim and are excluded from the new theorem.
All n=4 weighted-path D-optimal phase results are present in a published public record and are not new; the five-site symmetric phase and all-length weighted formula are separate.
The five-site mirror symmetry is a meaningful restricted family but the formula does not classify every arbitrary weighted path with simple global inequalities.

value.rationale: Full-state reachability volume is a natural D-optimal actuator placement invariant. For every arbitrary independently weighted path, the claim evaluates all candidate volumes and singular placements via explicit, rationally computable root-resultant edge polynomials, without numerically diagonalizing the diffusion generator or integrating over time. This structural lemma gives a new exact approach beyond prior unit-weight invariance and fixed n=4 weighted tables. The reflection-symmetric n=5 case has a sharp natural regime switch at equality of outer and inner conductances, with exactly the two endpoints optimal when b<a and exactly the adjacent interior pair optimal when b>a; all tie at equality while the center is always singular. This is a complete nontrivial design boundary, not a tiny numeric gain or unmotivated arbitrary parameter slice.
